The Petitioner has filed this petition against Respondents under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 18.12.2020 at about 6.15 p.m. Rudresh D. had been driving Auto bearing Reg.No.KA04D7386 on Ullala Main Road, Etto Basavanna Temple Circle,
SCCH5 Bengaluru, while turning the auto, a canter bearing Reg.No.KA04AA 0970 came in high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the auto,
due to the impact he fell down and sustained multiple injuries to his head and chest.
Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Rajarajeshwari Medical College and Hospital, wherein Doctor has declared him as dead.

2

Thereafter postmortem was conducted and handed over the body to the petitioner,
they have performed funeral rites by spending an amount of Rs.2,00,000/ for transportation and funeral ceremony.
3. At the time of accident, deceased/Rudresh D. was aged about 32 years, hale and healthy, he was working as auto driver, thereby earning Rs.60,000/ p.m.
Petitioner is sister of the deceased, due to sudden demise SCCH5 of the deceased, she has lost the earning member.
Out of this accident crime No.106/2020 is registered against the driver of the offending vehicle before the Kengeri Traffic Police.
R1 is driver, R2 is owner, R3 is insurer of the Canter Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA04 AA0970, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.82,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 24% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, R1 and R2/driver and owner have appeared but not filed written statement.
R3/insurer has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner.

The respondent company Malleshwaram Office has issued policy against the canter bearing Reg.No.KA 014AA0970 vide No.0716003119p112213595, which is valid since SCCH5 20.12.2019 to 19.12.2020, his liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.

Further submitted that, driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident, further vehicle had no valid permit and registration certificate to run on the road.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the deceased.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence the petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. On going through the rival pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following:

::ISSUES::
1.Whether the Petitioner proves that, deceased Late. Sri. Rudresh D. S/o.
SCCH5 Doddappa @ Doddayya was died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 18.12.2020 at about 6.15 p.m. near Ullala Main Road, near Etto Basavanna Temple Circle, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent driving of Canter vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA04 AA0970 by its driver, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove her case, petitioner/sister of the deceased has deposed her evidence as PW1 and got marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13.
On the other hand, counsel for R2 deposed that, he has no defence evidence.

3 7.
Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 :

As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8.
Issue No.1:
In order to prove her case, petitioner/sister of the deceased has deposed her evidence as PW1, in her chiefexamination she has reiterated the facts narrated in her petition.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of spot SCCH5 panchanama is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of inquest panchanama is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of statement of eyewitnesses are marked as Ex.P.7 to Ex.P.9.
9.
Major defence of the R3 is that, driver of the lorry had no driving licence, but in the case on hand copy of the DL is on record.
Further defence is that, there is no negligency of the lorry driver and very accident is occurred due to negligency of the auto driver, but such suggestion is denied by the PW1.
Further there is no denial about place, date and time of the accident.
Further defence is that,
petitioner
is not a sister of the deceased.
10. Police papers speaks that deceased had a sister by name Niveditha.
At the time of filing the petition, petitioner has filed petition in the name of Chayakumari, D/o.
Doddayya M.
As per the police SCCH5 papers, deceased had a sister by name Niveditha, D/o.
Doddayya M.
after cross examination with leave of the tribunal, amendment is carried out.
Accordingly name of the petitioner is written as Chayakumari @ Niveditha, but such order is not challenged by the R3 before the appellate court.
So that, said order is intact and come into force.
Further respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared, but not at all contested the petition.
Further police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the canter driver.
Considering the same, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in her favour.
Accordingly, I have answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:
As per the case of the petitioner, deceased/Rudresh D. was aged about 32 years at the SCCH5 time of accident.

In this regard she has produced DL extract marked as Ex.P.10,
wherein date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 29.10.1988, the alleged accident is occurred on 18.12.2020, hence relying on Ex.P.10, age of the deceased is considered as 33 years at the time of his death.
As per the case of the petitioner, deceased was auto driver, thereby earning Rs.60,000/ p.m.
to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.
Chayakumari.

4 12.
Petitioner is the sister of the deceased/Rudresh D.
in this regard she has produced aadhar card marked as Ex.P.11, it reveals that, she is daughter of Doddayya.
Further insupport of the same, she has furnished family tree issued by the Tahasildar, Bengaluru North Taluk marked at Ex.P.14, copy of ration SCCH5 card and also her PAN Card marked at Ex.P.15.
Further in crossexamination also PW1 stated that, she is none other than the real sister of the deceased.
13. On the other hand, there are police papers to show that, deceased had a sister by name Niveditha, but such any other women has filed petition for compensation.
During pendency of the petition, amendment is carried out stating that, petitioner is none other than the sister of the deceased and herself is called as Chayakumari @ Niveditha.
So that, considering the same this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner is none other than the real sister of the deceased.
Further it is noticed that, deceased was unmarried and he had lost his parents during his lifetime.
Under such circumstances, this tribunal comes SCCH5 to the conclusion that, petitioner is competent person to file this petition and claim for compensation.
14. As per case of the petitioner she is dependent on income of the deceased.

On careful perusal of the PAN card, aadhar card and police documents it is noticed that, petitioner is a married women,
even in cross examination she admits that, she is married and residing with her husband in Shivanagar Bengaluru since 5 years, her husband is working in irrigation department and getting salary.
Further admits that, there is no document to prove that, her husband had been assisting her financially.
Since date of marriage she is staying with her husband, she is not having any document to prove that, she was depending on income of her brother.
SCCH5 15.
Counsel for petitioner argued that, petitioner was depending on the income of the deceased, but to prove the said facts except the oral evidence, there is no documentary evidence on record.
She admits that, she is married and staying with her husband separately.
Under such circumstances, it goes to show that, petitioner was not dependent on the income of the deceased.
In supprot of his case, petitioner has not relied upon any citations.

16. On the other hand, counsel for R3 has relied upon judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the case of The United Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Rudrappa in MFA No.32334/2010 (MV) dated 11.09.2015 and relied upon para No.8 of the judgment, which reads as follows;
"Admittedly the petition was filed by Rudrappa, the father of the deceased and Gurulingamma, the mother of the deceased SCCH5 contending that they were dependeing on the inome of the deceased.

entities.text: United Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Rudrappa
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Both of them died during pendency of the petition.
As such, Channappa aged about 38 years, tailor by occupation, who is elder brother of the deceased came on record to prosecute the proceeding.
Since he was working as tailor having his own family consisting of wife and children, he cannot be called as dependent on the income of the deceased.
Rightly for the said reason he did not file a claim petition claiming compensation on account of the death of his brother.

It is only after the death of both the claimants/the parents, he came on Chayakumari.D.M vs Arun Kumar.K.N on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109548520/
5 record to prosecute the proceedings.
Since he is legal representative, he has a right to come on rcord to go on with the case.
However, in order to get compensation, what is relevant to be seen whether he was dependent on the income of the deceased.
Definitely he was not depending upon the income of the deceased.
Therefore, he did not SCCH5 go to file a claim petition.

Under such circumstances, he being a legal representative is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/ to be awarded under Sec.140 of M.V.Act towards loss of estate as held by the Supreme Court in a decision reported in 2007 (10) SCC 643 in case of Manjuri Bera V/s. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., and another.

entities.text: Manjuri Bera V/s. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The tribunal without going into this aspect straightly awarded compensation as if the claimant/Channappa was depending on the income of the deceased'.
17.

On perusal of the observation made and findings given by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above cited citation it is noticed that, when deceased has lost the parents, petitioner is brother of the deceased and he is having his separate family.
Under such circumstances, petitioner will not become dependent on SCCH5 the income of the deceased, so that, petitioner is not entitled for compensation as prays for.
He is entitled for compensation under Sec.140 of M.V.Act only for loss of estate.

So that, relying on the above said citation, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioner is entitled for loss of estate at the tune of Rs.75,000/.
18

. Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.75,000/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount,
19.

In the case on hand, respondent No.3 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.0716003119P112213595 which is valid since 20.12.2019 to 19.12.2020, the alleged accident was occurred on 18.12.2020 it reveals that, as on the date of SCCH5 accident, insurance policy was in force.
The driver of the offending vehicle had valid and effective driving license.
In this regard there is no dispute by the respondents.
So that, R3/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:

Inview of the above reasoning and discussions to the above issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.75,000/ (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand SCCH5 Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release entire award amount through epayment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
